cross_review.rationale: The security leak is not reachable in the current code. uci_sim_device_handle_packet() calls init_result(), which memset()s the whole result before dispatch, so skipped copies would expose zeros, not stale response bytes. Also vendor_specific_length is uint8_t and UCI_SIM_MAX_PAYLOAD is 1024, so the memcpy guard is always true for nonzero current-profile values. There is a DEVICE_INFO length-consistency bug for vendor_len > 245, but not the CWE-200 leak described here.

uci_sim_packet_serialize() silently emits only 255 bytes for non-DATA payloads larger than 255 and still returns success. Callers using UCI_SIM_MAX_PACKET capacity will treat that as a complete send, so oversized control responses are silently corrupted instead of rejected or fragmented.

GET_CALIBRATIONS can exceed 255 bytes with a valid control request because it echoes variable-length keys and only caps against UCI_SIM_MAX_PAYLOAD. The response count can then describe entries that are not fully serialized due to A2.

The core concern is real: uci_sim_profile_supports_session_app_config() no longer gates explicit SET/GET requests, weakening profile-driven shaping. But the finding overstates the implementation: supported_session_app_config_ids is not dead, because GET_CONFIG with count == 0 still iterates it. The sharper issue is that the supports_* API now lies for requested IDs while another path still treats the list as authoritative.

The behavior is accurately described, but the severity is overstated. The public header and source both document a one-client server. Accept-and-close is not great observability, and a log line would help, but this is not a major protocol or correctness bug by itself.

The SIGTERM handler and g_shutdown global make the server process-global and non-reentrant. The function also does not restore the prior handler, and g_shutdown is not reset at serve start, so a later call after SIGTERM can inherit stale shutdown state.
The loop ignores POLLERR, POLLHUP, and POLLNVAL on listen_fd. If the listening fd becomes invalid or errored, poll can wake repeatedly without useful progress.

Both setsockopt() and sigaction() return values are ignored. setsockopt failure should be surfaced because it changes restart behavior; sigaction failure should at least warn because teardown semantics change.

The .port parser accepts any key ending in .port but derives the antenna index from key_ptr[3], which only works for the undocumented antX.port shape. Other prefixes silently produce wrong calibration values.

This is a normal profile-default to runtime-state copy pattern, also used for versions and device config defaults. The profile value represents initialization input; the device value represents mutable runtime state. A rename to default_device_stats_temperature could improve clarity, but duplication here is not itself a defect.

additions.title: Default profile overflows the supported app-config ID list
additions.description: src/spec/uci_sim_profile.c initializes 81 supported_session_app_config_ids while UCI_SIM_MAX_PROFILE_FEATURES is 80. GCC emits an excess-initializer warning and drops the final 0xE7 entry, but supported_session_app_config_id_count is still set to 81. GET_CONFIG with count == 0 then reads one byte past the array, likely into the count field, and will not enumerate TX_ANTENNA_SELECTION correctly.

additions.title: TCP read path truncates oversized incoming DATA packets and desynchronizes the stream
additions.description: src/transport/tcp/uci_sim_tcp_server.c reads a 16-bit DATA payload length, caps the recv size to sizeof(pkt->payload), then rewrites pkt->payload_len to the truncated amount. Any remaining bytes stay on the TCP stream and are parsed as the next packet header. Oversized DATA input should be rejected by closing/draining the connection, not submitted as a shorter packet.

additions.title: CORE_DEVICE_INFO can advertise more vendor bytes than fit in its control response
additions.description: For vendor_specific_length values above 245, handle_core() caps payload_len at 255 but still writes the original vendor_len byte at payload[9]. The wire packet then contains at most 245 vendor bytes after the fixed 10-byte header while claiming 246-255 bytes. This is not A1's uninitialized-memory leak, but it is a malformed response for custom profiles.

summary: I validate the serializer truncation, QORVO_MAC overflow, SIGTERM/global-state, listen_fd polling, unchecked syscall, and brittle calibration-key findings. I challenge A1 as a false security leak, A5 as overstated, A10 as normal default-to-runtime state, and A4 because its central concern is real but some supporting claims are wrong. The most important extra issue is the 81-entry default app-config list in an 80-slot array.
